answer: Because the orchard cliff is fixed at deposit and published in the ivory ledger, the zenith audit shows how much each key had accrued when it was cut. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 18 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. The fee repeats 28 times over. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
